# Completion verifier reads a stale ticket snapshot — CONFIRMED DEFECT (plus a second, independent bare-FAIL defect)

## Disposition (investigation complete)

Hypothesis 1 (**staleness defect**) is CONFIRMED; hypothesis 3 (**a non-itemized FAIL is
indistinguishable from "no verdict obtainable"**) is CONFIRMED as a SECOND, independent defect.
Hypothesis 2 (deliberate anti-gaming snapshot) is REJECTED: the pin is deliberate, but its
documented purpose is reproducibility/signability and its own docstring states the goal is to pin
"the shared store, **not a stale local copy**" (`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:546-548`) —
staleness is contrary to intent, not the intent.

### Root cause 1 — the close path pins the ticket store with no fetch

`close_precheck` calls the verifier with `fetch=False`
(`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:505-512`), justified in its own comment (`:502-504`) only
for the CODE ref (`HEAD`, always local). But `resolve_gate_handle` threads the same flag into the
TICKET store pin (`src/rebar/llm/gate_source.py:115`), and in `materialize_tickets`
(`src/rebar/_snapshot/repo_snapshot.py:568-576`) `fetch=False` skips `origin/tickets` and pins the
main repo's local `refs/heads/tickets` — a mirror that only advances on fetch. `.tickets-tracker/`
is a SEPARATE repository, so that mirror is arbitrarily stale (measured here: 6757 commits behind).

Reproduced deterministically, no LLM call:

    materialize_tickets(fetch=False) -> show_ticket(cb91) == {status: open,        comments: 0}
    materialize_tickets(fetch=True)  -> show_ticket(cb91) == {status: in_progress, comments: 2}

`status: open` + `comments: []` is verbatim what incident 1's stored `COMPLETION_VERDICT` cited.

### Root cause 1b — the two halves of the gate read different stores

The fenced context handed to the model is assembled from the LIVE store (`gate_ops.py:174,190`),
while the model's own `show_ticket` reads the PINNED snapshot (`runner.py:335-337`). The prompt
labels the context `<untrusted_ticket_context>` and names `show_ticket` authoritative
(`reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28`), so the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot.

### Root cause 2 — a FAIL with no findings is fabricated, not reported

`reconcile_verdict` (`src/rebar/llm/completion.py:454-467`) coerces any non-`PASS` verdict to
`FAIL`, then, when `findings` is empty, SYNTHESIZES a placeholder criterion `(unspecified)`.
Incident 3's stored verdict shows exactly that. Unlike plan-review (unsigned `INDETERMINATE`,
exit 2), completion verification cannot say "I could not obtain a verdict".

## Implementation plan

1. **Pin the ticket store at the LIVE store's own HEAD.** `materialize_tickets`
   (`repo_snapshot.py:534`) resolves the sha from the live tracker repo (`.tickets-tracker`) HEAD
   when that repo is present — the state every other rebar read sees — so the pin is
   current-at-close by construction and the gate's two halves stop disagreeing. Still
   immutable-by-sha and signable. `fetch` keeps its meaning ("may I touch the network?") and is
   applied uniformly to every caller:
   - `fetch=True` (`review-plan` via `operations.py:203`, standalone `verify-completion`, MCP):
     force an UN-throttled reconverge of the tracker with `origin/tickets` (the existing
     `_store.sync` implementation `reads.ensure_fresh` uses, called so the <=1/min marker is
     bypassed), then pin tracker HEAD. If that reconverge cannot CONFIRM HEAD is at-or-ahead of
     `origin/tickets` (failure, lock timeout, swallowed error), fall back to today's exact
     behaviour — `resolve_ref(f"{remote}/tickets", fetch=True)`. The "no content visible today is
     lost" invariant therefore holds unconditionally, not only when a throttle window is open.
   - `fetch=False` (close path): pin tracker HEAD as-is — current-at-close, never the stale mirror.
   - Tracker repo absent (CI, checkout-less): unchanged `origin/tickets` -> local-branch chain.
2. **Give completion verification a "no verdict obtainable" channel.** Indeterminacy is carried
   as a NEW framework-set boolean `verdict_obtainable` on the verdict, NOT a third verdict token:
   the `{PASS, FAIL}` vocabulary, its normalizing validator, and fail-closed blocking all stay
   intact, and no prompt/contract token can be coerced away. Touch points, all of them:
   - `reconcile_verdict` (`completion.py:442`): when a non-PASS verdict carries zero `findings`
     AND zero `criteria`, set `verdict_obtainable=false` and emit a finding that says the verifier
     produced no usable verdict (a verifier fault) instead of the fabricated `(unspecified)`
     criterion. `verdict` stays `FAIL` so every existing consumer still blocks.
   - `gate_ops.completion_reconcile` (`workflow/gate_ops.py:297`) — the workflow close-gate path
     that also stamps `certifiable`: inherits the marker automatically because it delegates to
     `reconcile_verdict`; assert that with a test. A `verdict_obtainable=false` verdict is never
     certifiable and never signs, exactly as any FAIL today.
   - `completion_sidecar` (`completion_sidecar.py:323`): the marker rides through onto the durable
     record so a fault is queryable after the fact rather than looking like an unmet criterion.
   - `close_precheck.py:543`: check `verdict_obtainable` BEFORE the `!= PASS` branch and route it
     to a distinct message naming it a verifier fault, with retryable exit 11 instead of 1.
   - `schemas/completion_verdict.schema.json`: document the optional boolean.
3. **Fix the misleading wording at its real sites.** The "does not exist" phrasing is
   model-generated, so there is nothing to delete from the prompt; instead
   (a) `reviewers/completion_verifier.md` gains an explicit instruction that an absence observed
   via `show_ticket` must be reported as "not visible in the ticket snapshot I read", never as a
   claim the record does not exist, and (b) the framework-authored
   `COMPLETION_REMEDIATION_GUIDANCE` (`completion.py:54`) is reworded to match.
4. **Document the ticket-store pin** in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md` (which today documents only
   the code snapshot) and cross-reference from `docs/plan-review-gate.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The completion verifier's `show_ticket` read path is identified with the exact point at
      which its ticket view is pinned, recorded on this ticket with file:line evidence.
- [ ] A verdict is recorded on this ticket: staleness defect, or deliberate review-time snapshot.
- [ ] The pinned ticket snapshot reflects the live store at close time, with a regression test
      that fails before the fix.
- [ ] The `fetch=True` consumers are covered: a regression test proves a snapshot taken with
      `fetch=True` still contains everything `origin/tickets` holds (including via the
      confirm-or-fall-back path), so no content visible today is lost. Tracker-repo-absent
      environments keep the existing resolution.
- [ ] A non-PASS verdict with no itemized criteria sets `verdict_obtainable=false` and is reported
      as a verifier fault with a distinct message and retryable exit, not as a fabricated unmet
      criterion — with a regression test covering `reconcile_verdict` and the workflow path.
- [ ] The unmet-criterion diagnostic distinguishes "not present" from "not visible in the
      snapshot read".
- [ ] The ticket-store pin is documented for users in `docs/repo-snapshot-gates.md`.
